newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Police say S.African rape figures continue to rise.
newsitem.headline: Police say S.African rape figures continue to rise.

text.p: Reported rapes in South Africa, already the highest rate in the world, increased again in 1996, but police figures show murders, carjackings and other serious crimes declined slightly.
Police minister Sydney Mufamadi told a news conference he was encouraged that levels of reported crimes were declining, but added: "Crime levels in South Africa remain unacceptably high."
Reported rapes nationwide rose to 119.5 per 100,000 of the 42 million population last year compared with 115.2 for 1995.

Murders fell to 61.1 from 64.6 per 100,000 people, burglaries were nearly unchanged and carjackings fell some 18 percent in Gauteng region centred on Johannesburg -- the only province with comparable figures from previous years.
A total of 7,612 cases of carjackings, mostly at gun- or knife-point, were reported in the region last year.
Mufamadi said his ministry was encouraged by gains made by police over the past year.
"I am pleased to note that the majority of the 20 main serious crime categories continue to show a stabilising or declining trend in terms of reported cases," he added.
A police statistician told the briefing the increased rape figure might be a result of more cases being reported, rather than a rise in attacks.
Rape was a taboo subject in many communities and victims were reluctant to report cases but growing awareness of the problem is making women more confident about going to the police.
